name: New Mexico
summary: A red Zia sun symbol on a yellow field: a circle with four groups of four rays. The colours are those of Spain, and the symbol comes from the Zia Pueblo. It is often rated the best-designed US state flag.
origin: In 1920 the Daughters of the American Revolution held a design contest. The archaeologist and physician Harry Mera won with the Zia sun, based on a design on a 19th-century Zia Pueblo pot. The flag was adopted in 1925.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: From the flag of Spain, whose Crown ruled New Mexico.

symbols.name: Zia sun symbol
symbols.description: A circle with four groups of four rays.
symbols.meaning: The Zia Pueblo's sacred number four: the four directions, seasons, times of day and stages of life, bound together by a circle of life and love.

history.label: Early flag
history.note: Blue with the US flag and state seal.

facts: A 2001 NAVA survey ranked it the best-designed flag of any US state or Canadian province.
The Zia Pueblo has asked for recognition and compensation for the use of its sacred symbol.
New Mexico has an official 'salute to the flag' in English and Spanish.
clues: A red sun symbol with four groups of rays on yellow.
Its symbol comes from a pueblo's pottery.
Often voted the best-designed US state flag.
